title: The discrete forward theorem and the radius characterization

blocks.tex:
Dahlberg's forward theorem concerns a simple polygon whose vertices are locally
regular, including straight vertices. Its conclusion counts constant plateaux
correctly. The convex proof uses actual containing and interior-missing circles;
the remaining case uses the enclosing-circle construction detailed in the next
two chapters. Together these results prove the necessity in the paper's
circumradius characterization.

blocks.label: mf:core-defs
blocks.title: Local regularity and signed curvature
blocks.body:
Write $[A,B,C]=\operatorname{Im}(\overline{B-A}(C-A))$ and
\[
 k_i=\frac{2[P_{i-1},P_i,P_{i+1}]}
 {|P_i-P_{i-1}|\,|P_{i+1}-P_i|\,|P_{i+1}-P_{i-1}|}.
\]
A vertex is regular if it is straight and lies on the segment joining its
neighbours, or its positive-radius circumcircle has center in the closed
vertex cone
$P_i+\{s(P_{i-1}-P_i)+t(P_{i+1}-P_i):s,t\ge0\}$.
A polygon is regular when every vertex is regular. It is concyclic when all
vertices lie on a common circle of positive radius.

blocks.label: mf:core-extrema
blocks.title: Plateau-aware alternating extrema
blocks.body:
A local maximum at $i$ consists of integers $l,r>0$, $l+r\le n$, such that
$k_{i-m}=k_i$ for $0\le m<l$, $k_{i+m}=k_i$ for $0\le m<r$, and
$k_{i-l},k_{i+r}<k_i$. A local minimum reverses both strict inequalities.
The four-vertex condition requires integer representatives
$a<b<c<d<a+n$ at which there are, respectively, a local maximum, minimum,
maximum, and minimum. The representatives may lie inside extremal plateaux;
the strict exits ensure that different extremal runs are counted separately.

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.DahlbergFourVertex
lean.code:
def DahlbergFourVertex {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ : ℕ,
    i₁ < i₂ ∧ i₂ < i₃ ∧ i₃ < i₄ ∧ i₄ < i₁ + n ∧
      DiscreteLocalMax κ (i₁ : ZMod n) ∧
      DiscreteLocalMin κ (i₂ : ZMod n) ∧
      DiscreteLocalMax κ (i₃ : ZMod n) ∧
      DiscreteLocalMin κ (i₄ : ZMod n)

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.DiscreteLocalMin
lean.code:
def DiscreteLocalMin {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  ∃ l r : ℕ, 0 < l ∧ 0 < r ∧ l + r ≤ n ∧
    (∀ m < l, κ (i - (m : ZMod n)) = κ i) ∧
    (∀ m < r, κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) = κ i) ∧
    κ i < κ (i - (l : ZMod n)) ∧ κ i < κ (i + (r : ZMod n))

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.DiscreteLocalMax
lean.code:
def DiscreteLocalMax {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  ∃ l r : ℕ, 0 < l ∧ 0 < r ∧ l + r ≤ n ∧
    (∀ m < l, κ (i - (m : ZMod n)) = κ i) ∧
    (∀ m < r, κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) = κ i) ∧
    κ (i - (l : ZMod n)) < κ i ∧ κ (i + (r : ZMod n)) < κ i

blocks.label: mf:core-marked-maxima
blocks.title: Two disjoint families of weak maxima
blocks.body:
Let $k$ be a nonconstant cyclic word. Suppose $E,F$ are nonempty disjoint
sets of indices, every marked index is a weak maximum relative to its two
neighbours, and equality with either neighbour preserves membership in the
same marked set. Then $k$ has alternating plateau maxima and minima.

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.dahlbergFourVertex_of_two_disjoint_marked_weakMaxima
lean.code:
theorem dahlbergFourVertex_of_two_disjoint_marked_weakMaxima
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {P Q : ZMod n → Prop} {p q : ZMod n}
    (hpq : p ≠ q) (hPp : P p) (hQq : Q q)
    (hdisjoint : ∀ z, ¬ (P z ∧ Q z))
    (hweakP : ∀ z, P z → κ (z - 1) ≤ κ z ∧ κ (z + 1) ≤ κ z)
    (hpropPRight : ∀ z, P z → κ z = κ (z + 1) → P (z + 1))
    (hpropPLeft : ∀ z, P z → κ z = κ (z - 1) → P (z - 1))
    (hweakQ : ∀ z, Q z → κ (z - 1) ≤ κ z ∧ κ (z + 1) ≤ κ z)
    (hpropQRight : ∀ z, Q z → κ z = κ (z + 1) → Q (z + 1))
    (hpropQLeft : ∀ z, Q z → κ z = κ (z - 1) → Q (z - 1))
    (hnc : ¬ ∃ c, ∀ z : ZMod n, κ z = c) :
    DahlbergFourVertex κ := by
  let d : ℕ := (q - p).val
  let κ' : ZMod n → ℝ := fun z => κ (z + p)
  let P' : ZMod n → Prop := fun z => P (z + p)
  let Q' : ZMod n → Prop := fun z => Q (z + p)
  have hdpos : 0 < d := by
    apply Nat.pos_of_ne_zero
    intro hd0
    have hqp0 : q - p = 0 := (ZMod.val_eq_zero (q - p)).mp hd0
    apply hpq
    have := congrArg (fun z : ZMod n => z + p) hqp0
    simpa using this.symm
  have hdlt : d < n := ZMod.val_lt (q - p)
  have hdcast : (d : ZMod n) = q - p := by
    exact ZMod.natCast_zmod_val (q - p)
  have hP'0 : P' 0 := by simpa [P'] using hPp
  have hQ'd : Q' (d : ZMod n) := by
    dsimp [Q']
    rw [hdcast]
    convert hQq using 1
    abel
  have hdisjoint' : ∀ z, ¬ (P' z ∧ Q' z) := by
    intro z hz
    exact hdisjoint (z + p) hz
  have hweakP' : ∀ z, P' z →
      κ' (z - 1) ≤ κ' z ∧ κ' (z + 1) ≤ κ' z := by
    intro z hz
    rcases hweakP (z + p) hz with ⟨hl, hr⟩
    constructor
    · dsimp [κ']
      convert hl using 1
      abel_nf
    · dsimp [κ']
      convert hr using 1
      abel_nf
  have hpropP'Right : ∀ z, P' z →
      κ' z = κ' (z + 1) → P' (z + 1) := by
    intro z hz heq
    dsimp [P', κ'] at hz heq ⊢
    have hp := hpropPRight (z + p) hz (by
      convert heq using 1
      abel_nf)
    convert hp using 1
    abel
  have hpropP'Left : ∀ z, P' z →
      κ' z = κ' (z - 1) → P' (z - 1) := by
    intro z hz heq
    dsimp [P', κ'] at hz heq ⊢
  -- … (truncated)

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.exists_strict_drop_backward_of_marked_weakMax
lean.code:
theorem exists_strict_drop_backward_of_marked_weakMax
    {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {P : ZMod n → Prop} {a b : ℕ}
    (hab : a < b)
    (hPb : P (b : ZMod n)) (hnotPa : ¬ P (a : ZMod n))
    (hweakLeft : ∀ j, P j → κ (j - 1) ≤ κ j)
    (hpropLeft : ∀ j, P j → κ j = κ (j - 1) → P (j - 1)) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, a ≤ k ∧ k < b ∧ κ (k : ZMod n) < κ (b : ZMod n) := by
  let A : ZMod n := (a + b : ℕ)
  let μ : ZMod n → ℝ := fun z => κ (A - z)
  let Q : ZMod n → Prop := fun z => P (A - z)
  have hQa : Q (a : ZMod n) := by
    dsimp [Q, A]
    convert hPb using 1
    push_cast
    abel
  have hnotQb : ¬ Q (b : ZMod n) := by
    intro hQb
    apply hnotPa
    dsimp [Q, A] at hQb
    convert hQb using 1
    push_cast
    abel
  have hweakQ : ∀ z, Q z → μ (z + 1) ≤ μ z := by
    intro z hz
    dsimp [Q, μ] at hz ⊢
    convert hweakLeft (A - z) hz using 1
    abel_nf
  have hpropQ : ∀ z, Q z → μ z = μ (z + 1) → Q (z + 1) := by
    intro z hz heq
    dsimp [Q, μ] at hz heq ⊢
    have hp : P (A - z - 1) := hpropLeft (A - z) hz (by
      convert heq using 1
      abel_nf)
    convert hp using 1
    abel
  rcases exists_strict_drop_forward_of_marked_weakMax
      hab hQa hnotQb hweakQ hpropQ with ⟨k, hak, hkb, hdrop⟩
  refine ⟨a + b - k, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
  dsimp [μ, A] at hdrop
  have hk : k ≤ a + b := by omega
  have hidx : ((a + b - k : ℕ) : ZMod n) =
      ((a + b : ℕ) : ZMod n) - (k : ZMod n) := by
    rw [Nat.cast_sub hk]
  have hbidx : ((a + b : ℕ) : ZMod n) - (a : ZMod n) = (b : ZMod n) := by
    push_cast
    abel
  simpa [hidx, hbidx] using hdrop

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.discreteLocalMax_of_weak_neighbors_of_eq_propagates
lean.code:
theorem discreteLocalMax_of_weak_neighbors_of_eq_propagates
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {P : ZMod n → Prop} {i : ZMod n}
    (hPi : P i)
    (hweak : ∀ j, P j → κ (j - 1) ≤ κ j ∧ κ (j + 1) ≤ κ j)
    (hpropRight : ∀ j, P j → κ j = κ (j + 1) → P (j + 1))
    (hpropLeft : ∀ j, P j → κ j = κ (j - 1) → P (j - 1))
    (hnc : ¬ ∃ c, ∀ j : ZMod n, κ j = c) :
    DiscreteLocalMax κ i := by
  classical
  have hrightExists :
      ∃ r : ℕ, 0 < r ∧ r ≤ n ∧ κ (i + (r : ZMod n)) < κ i := by
    by_contra hnone
    have hplateau : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ n →
        κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) = κ i ∧ P (i + (m : ZMod n)) := by
      intro m hm
      induction m with
      | zero =>
          constructor
          · simp
          · simpa using hPi
      | succ m ih =>
          rcases ih (by omega) with ⟨hκm, hPm⟩
          have hle : κ (i + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n)) ≤ κ i := by
            simpa [Nat.cast_add, add_assoc, hκm] using (hweak _ hPm).2
          have heq : κ (i + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n)) = κ i := by
            apply le_antisymm hle
            apply le_of_not_gt
            intro hlt
            exact hnone ⟨m + 1, by omega, hm, hlt⟩
          refine ⟨heq, ?_⟩
          have hstep : κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) = κ (i + (m : ZMod n) + 1) := by
            rw [hκm]
            simpa [Nat.cast_add, add_assoc] using heq.symm
          simpa [Nat.cast_add, add_assoc] using hpropRight _ hPm hstep
    apply hnc
    refine ⟨κ i, fun j => ?_⟩
    let m : ℕ := (j - i).val
    have hmle : m ≤ n := (ZMod.val_lt (j - i)).le
    have hm := (hplateau m hmle).1
    have hidx : i + (m : ZMod n) = j := by
      dsimp [m]
      rw [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val (j - i)]
      abel
    simpa [hidx] using hm
  have hleftExists :
      ∃ l : ℕ, 0 < l ∧ l ≤ n ∧ κ (i - (l : ZMod n)) < κ i := by
    by_contra hnone
    have hplateau : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ n →
        κ (i - (m : ZMod n)) = κ i ∧ P (i - (m : ZMod n)) := by
      intro m hm
      induction m with
      | zero =>
          constructor
          · simp
          · simpa using hPi
      | succ m ih =>
          rcases ih (by omega) with ⟨hκm, hPm⟩
          have hle : κ (i - ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n)) ≤ κ i := by
            have hle' := (hweak _ hPm).1
            rw [hκm] at hle'
  -- … (truncated)

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.exists_strict_drop_forward_of_marked_weakMax
lean.code:
theorem exists_strict_drop_forward_of_marked_weakMax
    {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {P : ZMod n → Prop} {a b : ℕ}
    (hab : a < b)
    (hPa : P (a : ZMod n)) (hnotPb : ¬ P (b : ZMod n))
    (hweakRight : ∀ j, P j → κ (j + 1) ≤ κ j)
    (hpropRight : ∀ j, P j → κ j = κ (j + 1) → P (j + 1)) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, a < k ∧ k ≤ b ∧ κ (k : ZMod n) < κ (a : ZMod n) := by
  classical
  by_contra hnone
  have hwalk : ∀ t : ℕ, t ≤ b - a →
      κ (a + t : ZMod n) = κ (a : ZMod n) ∧ P (a + t : ZMod n) := by
    intro t ht
    induction t with
    | zero =>
        constructor
        · simp
        · simpa using hPa
    | succ t ih =>
        rcases ih (by omega) with ⟨hκt, hPt⟩
        have hle : κ (a + (t + 1) : ZMod n) ≤ κ (a : ZMod n) := by
          calc
            κ (a + (t + 1) : ZMod n) = κ ((a + t : ZMod n) + 1) := by
              congr 1
              ring
            _ ≤ κ (a + t : ZMod n) := hweakRight _ hPt
            _ = κ (a : ZMod n) := hκt
        have hnotlt : ¬ κ (a + (t + 1) : ZMod n) < κ (a : ZMod n) := by
          intro hlt
          apply hnone
          refine ⟨a + (t + 1), by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
          simpa [Nat.cast_add] using hlt
        have heq : κ (a + (t + 1) : ZMod n) = κ (a : ZMod n) :=
          le_antisymm hle (le_of_not_gt hnotlt)
        have heq' : κ (a + (t + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) = κ (a : ZMod n) := by
          simpa only [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using heq
        refine ⟨heq', ?_⟩
        have hstep : κ (a + t : ZMod n) = κ ((a + t : ZMod n) + 1) := by
          rw [hκt]
          simpa only [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, add_assoc] using heq.symm
        simpa only [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, add_assoc] using hpropRight _ hPt hstep
  have hend := (hwalk (b - a) (by omega)).2
  have hab_le : a ≤ b := Nat.le_of_lt hab
  rw [← Nat.cast_add, Nat.add_sub_of_le hab_le] at hend
  exact hnotPb hend

blocks.tex:
Starting at an index in $E$, continue through equal values in each direction.
Nonconstancy prevents this process from traversing the whole cycle. At the
first unequal value the weak maximum inequality makes the exit a strict drop;
equality propagation keeps the entire run in $E$. Repeat for $F$. The runs
are disjoint. On each complementary arc use the strict exit from each of
its two bounding maximum runs. The minimum of the finite arc is therefore
below both endpoint values and lies in its interior;
extending through ties gives a plateau minimum with strict rises on both
sides. The two complementary arcs give the required alternating minima.

blocks.label: mf:core-circle-coordinates
blocks.title: Circle coordinates along a chord
blocks.body:
Translate and rotate a nonzero chord so its endpoints are $-a,a$, with $a>0$.
A circle through them has center $iy$ and radius $\sqrt{a^2+y^2}$.
For a third point $z=x+it$ with $t\ne0$, its circumcircle parameter is
\[
 y_z=\frac{x^2+t^2-a^2}{2t},\qquad
 \operatorname{power}_{y}(z)=x^2+t^2-2yt-a^2.
\]
Its signed curvature is
$\operatorname{sign}(t)/\sqrt{a^2+y_z^2}$, using the chord ordering.
Regularity at either chord endpoint, for the incident triple containing $z$,
selects the nonnegative parameter on the positive-turn branch and the
nonpositive parameter on the negative-turn branch.

theorem signedMengerR2_edge_parameter {A B C : ℂ} (hAB : A ≠ B)
    (hcross : Gluck.Discrete.crossR2 A B C ≠ 0) :
    Gluck.Discrete.signedMengerR2 A B C =
      ((edgeCoordinates A B C).im / |(edgeCoordinates A B C).im|) *
        normalizedCircleCurvature (chordHalfLength A B) (edgeCircumcenterParameter A B C) := by
  have hz := edgeCoordinates_im_ne_zero hAB hcross
  have hi := signedMengerR2_directIsometry (norm_chordUnit hAB) (chordMidpoint A B)
    (-chordHalfLength A B : ℂ) (chordHalfLength A B : ℂ) (edgeCoordinates A B C)
  have he := canonicalChord_endpoints hAB
  unfold transportedChordLeft transportedChordRight at he
  rw [he.1, he.2, directIsometryR2_edgeCoordinates hAB] at hi
  have hn := signedMengerR2_normalized (chordHalfLength_pos hAB) hz
  simpa [edgeCircumcenterParameter] using hi.trans hn

blocks.tex:
The difference of the squared distances to $a$ and $-a$ forces the center's
real part to vanish. Equidistance to $z$ gives the displayed linear equation
for $y_z$. The signed Menger formula and the circle radius identity give the
curvature. Expressing the center as a nonnegative combination of the two
incident edge vectors gives the asserted parameter sign. Thus on each
regular branch equality of curvature determines the parameter uniquely.

blocks.label: mf:core-rigidity
blocks.title: Constant curvature forces a common circle
blocks.body:
For a simple locally regular polygon, equal nonzero curvature at adjacent
vertices gives the same circumcircle. Consequently a constant nonzero
profile makes the polygon concyclic; the identically zero profile is
impossible. Conversely a positively oriented simple concyclic polygon has
constant curvature $1/R$.

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.not_constant_signedMengerProfile_of_not_concyclic
lean.code:
theorem not_constant_signedMengerProfile_of_not_concyclic
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {v : ZMod n → ℂ}
    (hsimple : Gluck.Discrete.IsSimplePolygon v) (hregular : DahlbergRegular v)
    (hnoncircle : ¬ Concyclic v) :
    ¬ ∃ c, ∀ i : ZMod n, SignedMengerProfile v i = c := by
  rintro ⟨c, hc⟩
  have hc0 : c = 0 :=
    constant_signedMengerProfile_eq_zero_of_not_concyclic hsimple hregular hnoncircle hc
  have hκzero : ∀ i : ZMod n, SignedMengerProfile v i = 0 := by
    intro i
    exact (hc i).trans hc0
  exact not_constant_signedMengerProfile_zero_of_isSimplePolygon hsimple hregular hκzero

theorem not_constant_signedMengerProfile_zero_of_isSimplePolygon {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]

  have hC :
      Gluck.Discrete.crossR2 (v (0 : ZMod n)) (v ((0 : ZMod n) + 1)) (v i) = 0 :=

    all_vertices_cross_eq_zero_of_constant_signedMengerProfile_zero hsimple hκ 0 (i + 1)
  have hvi : v i = v (i + 1) :=
    eq_of_crossR2_eq_zero_of_lineCoordR2_eq hbase hC hD hcoord

lean.code:
theorem edgeCommonCircumcircle_of_endpoint_regular_neg_eq {A B P Q : ℂ}
    (hAB : A ≠ B)
    (hPcross : Gluck.Discrete.crossR2 A B P < 0)
    (hQcross : Gluck.Discrete.crossR2 A B Q < 0)

The common edge supplies one chord coordinate system. Equal curvature and
the regularity sign restriction give equal center parameters, hence equal
centers and radii. Propagate this equality through the finite cycle. If the

the middle vertex between its neighbours. Consecutive nonzero edges then

word, together with this betweenness condition, forces equality across an
adjacent edge, contradicting simplicity. The converse follows from the
positive signed-curvature formula on the common circle.

blocks.tex:
Use the outgoing edge as the chord. All other vertices have positive height
$t$ in its oriented coordinates. Choose the minimum of their finitely many
parameters $y_z$. The inequality $y\le y_z$ is exactly nonnegative circle
power, so every vertex lies outside or on the circle; a minimizing third
vertex supplies the third contact. For localization, subtract the powers of
two circles. The result is affine. At the endpoints of a gap in one contact
set its sign is opposite to the strict sign at the interior contact of the
other circle. If the second circle had a contact outside the gap, strict
convex chord separation would give a chord intersection where the two affine
sign calculations contradict each other. This is the containing argument
with the power inequalities reversed.

blocks.tex:
An interior-missing local circumdisk has radius no greater than the two
neighbouring circumradii: compare the circle powers in each common chord
coordinate system. Positive reciprocal curvature therefore makes it a weak
local maximum. Mark all indices having the first selected circle's complete
center-radius data, and separately those having the second circle's data.
The sets are nonempty and disjoint. Adjacent equal curvature propagates the
entire circle data by rigidity, so the marked sets satisfy equality
propagation. Nonconcyclicity makes the profile nonconstant. Apply the
marked-maxima lemma to obtain the two genuine plateaux and their intervening
minima. This step supplies strict plateau exits even when consecutive
curvatures are equal.

blocks.label: mf:core-two-arcs
blocks.title: The alternative when four extrema are absent
blocks.body:
If a nonconstant cyclic word has no alternating plateau maxima and minima,
choose a global minimum and a global maximum. The word is weakly increasing
on the oriented arc from the minimum to the maximum and weakly decreasing
on the complementary arc. Every nonempty sublevel set $\{i:k_i\le t\}$ is
a cyclic interval, including the nonpositive set at $t=0$.

theorem dahlbergFourVertex_of_descent_between_globalMinMax
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {a b : ℕ}

    (hminA : ∀ z : ZMod n, κ (a : ZMod n) ≤ κ z)
    (hmaxB : ∀ z : ZMod n, κ z ≤ κ (b : ZMod n))
    (hdesc : ∃ k : ℕ, a ≤ k ∧ k < b ∧
      κ (k + 1 : ZMod n) < κ (k : ZMod n)) :
    DahlbergFourVertex κ := by
  rcases hdesc with ⟨k, hak, hkb, hdesc⟩
  have hnc : ¬ ∃ c, ∀ z : ZMod n, κ z = c := by
    rintro ⟨c, hc⟩
    rw [hc (k + 1 : ZMod n), hc (k : ZMod n)] at hdesc
    exact (lt_irrefl c) hdesc
  have hncNeg : ¬ ∃ c, ∀ z : ZMod n, -κ z = c :=
    not_constant_neg_iff.mpr hnc
  have hA_lt_k : κ (a : ZMod n) < κ (k : ZMod n) :=
    (hminA (k + 1 : ZMod n)).trans_lt hdesc
  have hkp1_lt_B : κ (k + 1 : ZMod n) < κ (b : ZMod n) :=
    hdesc.trans_le (hmaxB (k : ZMod n))
  have hleftA : ∃ t : ℕ, a ≤ t ∧ t ≤ k + 1 ∧
      -κ (t : ZMod n) < -κ (a : ZMod n) :=
    ⟨k, hak, by omega, neg_lt_neg hA_lt_k⟩
  have hleftB : ∃ t : ℕ, a ≤ t ∧ t ≤ k + 1 ∧
      -κ (t : ZMod n) < -κ ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) :=
    ⟨k, hak, by omega, by simpa [Nat.cast_add] using neg_lt_neg hdesc⟩
  obtain ⟨p, hap, hpk, hminNeg⟩ :=
    exists_discreteLocalMin_between_of_strictly_below_endpoints
      (κ := fun z => -κ z) (a := a) (b := k + 1)
      (by omega) hleftA hleftB hncNeg
  have hmaxP : DiscreteLocalMax κ (p : ZMod n) :=
    discreteLocalMax_of_neg_localMin hminNeg
  have hrightA : ∃ t : ℕ, k ≤ t ∧ t ≤ b ∧
      κ (t : ZMod n) < κ (k : ZMod n) :=
    ⟨k + 1, by omega, by omega, by simpa [Nat.cast_add] using hdesc⟩
  have hrightB : ∃ t : ℕ, k ≤ t ∧ t ≤ b ∧
      κ (t : ZMod n) < κ (b : ZMod n) :=
    ⟨k + 1, by omega, by omega, by simpa [Nat.cast_add] using hkp1_lt_B⟩
  obtain ⟨m, hkm, hmb, hminM⟩ :=
    exists_discreteLocalMin_between_of_strictly_below_endpoints
      (κ := κ) (a := k) (b := b) hkb hrightA hrightB hnc
  have hminA_local : DiscreteLocalMin κ (a : ZMod n) :=
    discreteLocalMin_of_globalMin_of_not_constant hminA hnc
  have hmaxB_local : DiscreteLocalMax κ (b : ZMod n) :=
    discreteLocalMax_of_globalMax_of_not_constant hmaxB hnc
  have hcast : ((a + n : ℕ) : ZMod n) = (a : ZMod n) := by
    rw [Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_self, add_zero]
  exact ⟨p, m, b, a + n, by omega, hmb, hwrap, by omega,
    hmaxP, hminM, hmaxB_local, by simpa [hcast] using hminA_local⟩

def WeaklyDecreasingLift {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=

def TwoArcMonotone {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ)
    (qmin qmax : ZMod n) : Prop :=
  let d := (qmax - qmin).val
  0 < d ∧ d < n ∧
    WeaklyIncreasingLift (fun z => κ (z + qmin)) 0 d ∧
    WeaklyDecreasingLift (fun z => κ (z + qmin)) d n

def WeaklyIncreasingLift {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=

theorem exists_globalMinMax_twoArcMonotone_and_nonpositiveConnected
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hnc : ¬ ∃ c, ∀ z : ZMod n, κ z = c)
    (hnot : ¬ DahlbergFourVertex κ)
    (hnonpos : ∃ z : ZMod n, κ z ≤ 0) :
    ∃ qmin qmax : ZMod n,
      (∀ z : ZMod n, κ qmin ≤ κ z) ∧
      (∀ z : ZMod n, κ z ≤ κ qmax) ∧
      κ qmin < κ qmax ∧
      TwoArcMonotone κ qmin qmax ∧
      Gluck.IsCyclicInterval (NonpositiveVertices κ) := by
  obtain ⟨qmin, qmax, hmin, hmax, hlt, htwo⟩ :=
    exists_globalMinMax_twoArcMonotone_of_not_dahlberg hnc hnot
  rcases hnonpos with ⟨z, hz⟩
  have hminNonpos : κ qmin ≤ 0 := (hmin z).trans hz
  exact ⟨qmin, qmax, hmin, hmax, hlt, htwo,
    nonpositiveVertices_isCyclicInterval_of_twoArcMonotone hminNonpos htwo⟩

blocks.tex:
A strict descent on the minimum-to-maximum arc supplies an interior maximum
before the descent and an interior minimum after it, by finite extremization
and extension through equal values. Together with the global extrema these
would give the forbidden four-vertex pattern. Thus every adjacent comparison
on that arc is increasing. Reverse the argument on the other arc. On each
monotone arc a sublevel set is an initial or terminal interval; their union
joins at the minimum and is therefore one cyclic interval. For a general
threshold apply this argument to $k-t$; translation of the values preserves
the plateau condition and nonconstancy. Translating the
cyclic cut back to the original labels preserves this statement.

blocks.label: mf:core-reversal
blocks.title: Reversing orientation preserves the conclusion
blocks.body:
Negating a cyclic word interchanges plateau maxima and minima. Reversing its
cyclic indexing reverses their order. Both operations preserve the existence
of an alternating four-vertex pattern. Reversing polygon traversal preserves
simplicity, regularity and nonconcyclicity and changes the curvature word to
$-k_{-i}$, so the convex theorem also covers an everywhere negative orientation.

Transport each constant plateau and its two strict exits through the change
of labels, and rotate the four chosen representatives if necessary so a
maximum comes first. Swapping the outer vertices of a Menger triple negates

For $n\ge4$, every simple locally regular nonconcyclic Euclidean polygon has
two plateau maxima and two plateau minima of its signed Menger curvature,
alternating around the polygon.

blocks.tex:
If all turns have the same strict sign, apply the convex result after
reversing traversal if needed. In the remaining case suppose that the
conclusion fails. Rigidity first rules out a constant profile, and the
combinatorial alternative gives the two monotone arcs and connected
nonpositive set. A minimal enclosing disk has positive radius. The contact
selection and orientation lemmas produce a nonempty positive chain between
contacts with interior curvature greater than the disk curvature. The actual
circle-splice construction closes this chain to a simple positively oriented
nonconcyclic polygon. Its containing-disk radius contradiction
is impossible. Each geometric input is constructed in the cited supporting
chapters; the final result has no unproduced circle-source hypothesis.

blocks.label: mf:core-threshold-extrema
blocks.title: Four plateau extrema yield a strict level window
blocks.body:
A word with alternating plateau maxima and minima admits four cyclically
ordered indices with values strictly above, below, above, below one common
level. The lower indices may be different from the initially chosen minima.

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.not_localMin_on_left_max_plateau
lean.code:
lemma not_localMin_on_left_max_plateau {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {i : ZMod n} {l d : ℕ}
    (hd : d < l) (heq : ∀ m < l, κ (i - (m : ZMod n)) = κ i)
    (hdrop : κ (i - (l : ZMod n)) < κ i) :
    ¬ DiscreteLocalMin κ (i - (d : ZMod n)) := by
  intro hmin
  apply not_localMin_on_right_max_plateau (κ := fun j ↦ κ (-j)) (i := -i) hd
  · intro m hm
    simpa only [neg_add_rev, neg_neg, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using heq m hm
  · simpa only [neg_add_rev, neg_neg, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm] using hdrop
  · convert discreteLocalMin_negIndex hmin using 1
    abel

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.alternatesAcrossLevel_of_lower_localMax
lean.code:
lemma alternatesAcrossLevel_of_lower_localMax {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {a b c d : ℕ}
    (hab : a < b) (hbc : b < c) (hcd : c < d) (hda : d < a + n)
    (hmax : DiscreteLocalMax κ (a : ZMod n))
    (hminb : DiscreteLocalMin κ (b : ZMod n))
    (hmind : DiscreteLocalMin κ (d : ZMod n)) (hac : κ (a : ZMod n) ≤ κ (c : ZMod n)) :
    ∃ z, AlternatesAcrossLevel κ z := by
  obtain ⟨l, r, hl, hr, hlr, hleft, hright, hldrop, hrdrop⟩ := hmax
  have hrb : r ≤ b - a := by
    by_contra h
    have hidx : (a : ZMod n) + ((b - a : ℕ) : ZMod n) = (b : ZMod n) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hab.le]
      ring
    exact not_localMin_on_right_max_plateau (d := b - a) (by omega) hright hrdrop
      (by simpa only [hidx] using hminb)
  have hld : l ≤ a + n - d := by
    by_contra h
    have hidx : (a : ZMod n) - ((a + n - d : ℕ) : ZMod n) = (d : ZMod n) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hda.le, Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_self]
      ring
    exact not_localMin_on_left_max_plateau (d := a + n - d) (by omega) hleft hldrop
      (by simpa only [hidx] using hmind)
  let m := max (κ ((a : ZMod n) - (l : ZMod n))) (κ ((a : ZMod n) + (r : ZMod n)))
  have hm : m < κ (a : ZMod n) := max_lt hldrop hrdrop
  refine ⟨(m + κ (a : ZMod n)) / 2, a, a + r, c, a + (n - l),
    by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have hh := le_max_right (κ ((a : ZMod n) - (l : ZMod n)))
      (κ ((a : ZMod n) + (r : ZMod n)))
    rw [Nat.cast_add]
    change κ ((a : ZMod n) + (r : ZMod n)) ≤ m at hh
    linarith
  · have hh := le_max_left (κ ((a : ZMod n) - (l : ZMod n)))
      (κ ((a : ZMod n) + (r : ZMod n)))
    rw [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_sub (show l ≤ n by omega), ZMod.natCast_self, zero_sub]
    change κ ((a : ZMod n) - (l : ZMod n)) ≤ m at hh
    rw [← sub_eq_add_neg]
    linarith
  · linarith
  · linarith

theorem DahlbergFourVertex.exists_alternatesAcrossLevel {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (h : DahlbergFourVertex κ) : ∃ z, AlternatesAcrossLevel κ z := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, d, hab, hbc, hcd, hda, hma, hmb, hmc, hmd⟩ := h
  rcases le_total (κ (a : ZMod n)) (κ (c : ZMod n)) with hac | hca
  · exact alternatesAcrossLevel_of_lower_localMax hab hbc hcd hda hma hmb hmd hac
  · apply alternatesAcrossLevel_of_lower_localMax hcd hda (Nat.add_lt_add_right hab n)
      (by omega) hmc hmd
    · simpa only [Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_self, add_zero] using hmb
    · simpa only [Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_self, add_zero] using hca

  exact ⟨z, a, b, c, d, hab, hbc, hcd, hda, ha, hb, hc, hd⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Forward.not_localMin_on_right_max_plateau
lean.code:
lemma not_localMin_on_right_max_plateau {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {i : ZMod n} {r d : ℕ}
    (hd : d < r) (heq : ∀ m < r, κ (i + (m : ZMod n)) = κ i)
    (hdrop : κ (i + (r : ZMod n)) < κ i) :
    ¬ DiscreteLocalMin κ (i + (d : ZMod n)) := by
  rintro ⟨l, s, hl, hs, hn, hleft, hright, hlrise, hrise⟩
  have hdval := heq d hd
  by_cases hds : d + s < r
  · have he := heq (d + s) hds
    rw [Nat.cast_add, ← add_assoc] at he
    rw [he, hdval] at hrise
    exact (lt_irrefl _ hrise)
  · have hrs : r - d ≤ s := by omega
    rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hrs with hrs | hrs
    · have he := hright (r - d) hrs
      have hidx : i + (d : ZMod n) + ((r - d : ℕ) : ZMod n) = i + (r : ZMod n) := by
        rw [Nat.cast_sub hd.le]
        ring
      rw [hidx, hdval] at he
      exact (ne_of_lt hdrop) he
    · have hidx : i + (d : ZMod n) + (s : ZMod n) = i + (r : ZMod n) := by
        rw [← hrs, Nat.cast_sub hd.le]
        ring
      rw [hidx, hdval] at hrise
      exact (not_lt_of_gt hdrop) hrise

blocks.tex:
Choose the smaller of the two maximum values, say $k_a\le k_c$. The constant
plateau through $a$ cannot contain either adjacent chosen minimum, because
a local minimum requires strict rises at its two exits. Its first strict
left and right drops therefore occur at or before those minima, one in each arc
between $a$ and $c$. Let $m$ be the larger of the two drop values. Then
$m<k_a\le k_c$, and the level $(m+k_a)/2$ separates both maxima from both
drops. Place these four indices in cyclic order. Their strict inequalities
are exactly the level-window condition, equivalently the required DFV
ordering after shifting and naming the low and high sites consistently.

blocks.label: mf:core-plateau
blocks.title: The plateau-run condition
blocks.body:
Alternating plateau extrema give two distinct maximal plateau maximum runs
and two distinct maximal plateau minimum runs. For a positive cyclic word,
reciprocation preserves this four-vertex property while interchanging maxima
and minima.

deps.title: Four plateau extrema yield a strict level window
deps.label: mf:core-threshold-extrema

blocks.tex:
Use the strict level window to select a maximum on each of its two disjoint
high arcs and a minimum on each low arc. Extend through equal values to
maximal constant runs. The separating strict inequalities keep the two
maximum runs distinct and likewise the minimum runs. This is precisely the
existing DFV-to-plateau-extrema lemma. On positive numbers $x\mapsto1/x$ is
strictly decreasing and injective, so constant runs remain the same and every
strict exit reverses direction. Rotate the alternating extrema accordingly.

blocks.label: mf:core-coherence
blocks.title: Coherence supplies the forward hypotheses
blocks.body:
A coherent strictly convex polygon is locally regular and positively
oriented. Its vertex circumradius is $r_i=1/k_i$, with $k_i>0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsCoherentConvexPolygon.vertexCircumradius_eq_inv
lean.code:
lemma IsCoherentConvexPolygon.vertexCircumradius_eq_inv {v : ZMod n → ℂ}
    (h : IsCoherentConvexPolygon v) (i : ZMod n) :
    vertexCircumradius v i = 1 / SignedMengerProfile v i := by
  rw [vertexCircumradius, dist_circumcenterR2_eq_inv_abs_signedMenger ((h.2.2 i).1),
    abs_of_pos (signedMengerR2_pos_iff_crossR2_pos.mpr (h.positivePolygonOrientation i))]
  rfl

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.CoherentR2.dahlbergRegular
lean.code:
lemma CoherentR2.dahlbergRegular {v : ZMod n → ℂ} (h : CoherentR2 v) :
    DahlbergRegular v := by
  intro i
  have hi := (h i).1
  have he := circumcenterR2_equidist hi
  have hp := pairwise_ne_of_crossR2_ne_zero hi
  have hR : 0 < vertexCircumradius v i := by
    apply dist_pos.mpr
    intro hc
    have hd := he.1
    rw [hc, dist_self] at hd
    exact hp.1 (dist_eq_zero.mp hd)
  obtain ⟨s, t, hs, ht, hC⟩ := (h i).2
  refine Or.inr ⟨circumcenterR2 (v i) (v (i - 1)) (v (i + 1)),
    vertexCircumradius v i, ⟨hR, he.1, rfl, he.2⟩, s, t, hs.le, ht.le, ?_⟩
  rw [hC]
  ring

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsCoherentConvexPolygon.positivePolygonOrientation
lean.code:
lemma IsCoherentConvexPolygon.positivePolygonOrientation {v : ZMod n → ℂ}
    (h : IsCoherentConvexPolygon v) : PositivePolygonOrientation v := by
  intro i
  have hp := pairwise_ne_of_crossR2_ne_zero ((h.2.2 i).1)
  have ha : i + 1 ≠ i - 1 := by
    intro he
    exact hp.2.1 (congrArg v he).symm
  have hb : i + 1 ≠ i - 1 + 1 := by
    intro he
    exact hp.2.2 (congrArg v (by simpa only [sub_add_cancel] using he))
  simpa only [sub_add_cancel] using h.2.1 (i - 1) (i + 1) ha hb

blocks.tex:
Coherence places the actual circumcenter in the open vertex cone, hence in
the closed cone required by regularity. Noncollinearity gives a genuine
positive circumradius. Strict global edge support applied to the third
vertex makes every local cross product positive. The circumradius identity
is $r_i=1/|k_i|$; positivity removes the absolute value.

blocks.label: mf:core-iff
blocks.title: Exact characterization of positive nonconstant circumradii
blocks.body:
Let $n\ge4$ and let $r$ be a positive nonconstant cyclic word. There exists a
coherent strictly convex polygon with vertex circumradii exactly $r_i$ if
and only if $r$ has two distinct plateau maximum runs and two distinct
plateau minimum runs.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tabachnikov_radius_characterization
lean.code:
theorem tabachnikov_radius_characterization [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) {r : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i) (hnc : ¬ ∃ c, ∀ i, r i = c) :
    (∃ v : ZMod n → ℂ, IsCoherentConvexPolygon v ∧
      ∀ i, vertexCircumradius v i = r i) ↔ IsPlateauTwoMaxTwoMin r := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, hrad⟩
    have hnoncircle : ¬ Concyclic v := by
      intro hcircle
      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_constant_signedMengerProfile_of_concyclic_positiveOrientation
        hv.1 hcircle hv.positivePolygonOrientation
      apply hnc
      refine ⟨1 / c, fun i ↦ ?_⟩
      rw [← hrad i, hv.vertexCircumradius_eq_inv i, hc i]
    have hfv := dahlberg_discrete_four_vertex_E2 hn v hv.1 hv.2.2.dahlbergRegular hnoncircle
    have hpos : ∀ i, 0 < SignedMengerProfile v i := fun i ↦
      signedMengerR2_pos_iff_crossR2_pos.mpr (hv.positivePolygonOrientation i)
    have hinv := dahlbergFourVertex_inv_of_pos hpos hfv
    have heq : ∀ i, r i = (SignedMengerProfile v i)⁻¹ := by
      intro i
      rw [← hrad i, hv.vertexCircumradius_eq_inv i, one_div]
    exact (dahlbergFourVertex_congr heq hinv).hasTwoPlateauMaxRuns_and_min
  · exact tabachnikov_converse_geometric hn hr

deps.title: Constant curvature forces a common circle
deps.label: mf:core-rigidity

blocks.tex:
Given a realizing polygon, coherence supplies local regularity and positive
orientation. If the polygon were concyclic, its positive signed curvature
would be constant, hence so would its reciprocal radius word, contrary to
the hypothesis. Apply the full discrete forward theorem, then reciprocate
its positive curvature profile and use the plateau-run bridge. This proves
necessity for exactly the prescribed radii. Conversely, the paper's
Tabachnikov converse constructs a coherent strictly convex polygon with
those radii from the plateau condition. Nonconstancy is part of this
characterization; constant circles belong to the separate constant case.
